items.title: Election of three members of the Company’s Board of Directors with terms to expire in 2026
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to elect three director nominees: Christopher E. Cragg, Katheryn B. Curtis, and Alaina K. Brooks, each for a term expiring in 2026. The Board recommends voting FOR each nominee.

items.title: Advisory approval of the Company’s executive compensation
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve, on a non-binding advisory basis, the compensation of the Company’s executives as disclosed in the proxy statement. The Board recommends voting FOR this proposal.

items.title: Selection of frequency of say-on-pay votes
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to select, on an advisory basis, whether the Company should conduct future say-on-pay votes every one year, two years, or three years. The Board recommends voting for the option to have a say-on-pay vote every year.

items.title: Approval of an amendment to the Company’s 2014 Equity Incentive Plan to extend the term by five years and increase shares by 600,000
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve an amendment to the 2014 Equity Incentive Plan to extend its term by five years and increase the number of shares available under the plan by 600,000 shares for a total of 1,350,000 shares. The Board recommends voting FOR the approval of the amendment. Approval requires the affirmative vote of a majority of shares present or represented at the meeting.
items.approvalStandard: Majority of shares entitled to vote and represented at the meeting

items.title: Approval of an amendment to increase the maximum number of authorized shares of common and preferred stock
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve an amendment to the Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation to increase the maximum number of authorized shares of common stock from 200,000,000 to 400,000,000 and preferred stock from 25,000,000 to 100,000,000. This will provide the company flexibility for future issuances for various corporate purposes.
items.approvalStandard: Majority of total outstanding shares entitled to vote

items.title: Approval of an amendment to remove the restriction on stockholder action by written consent
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve an amendment to the Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation to remove the current restriction that prohibits stockholder action by written consent, allowing stockholders to take action without a meeting by written consent.
items.approvalStandard: Majority of total outstanding shares entitled to vote

items.title: Election of eight directors to serve until the 2024 Annual Meeting
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to elect eight directors to serve until the 2024 Annual Meeting and thereafter until their successors are elected and qualified. Directors are elected annually by a majority vote standard.

items.title: Advisory vote to approve executive officer compensation
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve, on a non-binding advisory basis, the compensation of the named executive officers as disclosed in the proxy statement, including the Compensation Discussion and Analysis and compensation tables.

items.title: Advisory vote on the frequency of future advisory votes to approve named executive officer compensation
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to provide a non-binding advisory vote on the desired frequency (one, two, or three years) for future advisory votes to approve named executive officer compensation. The option receiving a plurality of votes will be deemed the preferred frequency.

items.title: Ratification of independent registered public accounting firm
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to ratify the appointment of Deloitte & Touche LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2023.

items.title: Election of three Class II director nominees for three-year terms
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to elect three Class II directors nominated by the board to serve until the 2026 annual meeting of stockholders. The nominees are Charles Bland, Stephen Daly, and Susan Ocampo. Proxies will be voted for these nominees unless stockholders indicate otherwise.

items.title: Advisory vote to approve the compensation of named executive officers
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve, on an advisory basis, the compensation paid to the named executive officers for fiscal year 2022.

items.title: Ratification of appointment of Deloitte & Touche LLP as independent registered public accounting firm
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to ratify the appointment of Deloitte & Touche LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending September 29, 2023.

items.title: Approval of amendment to the Company’s Fifth Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation to reflect Delaware law provisions allowing officer exculpation
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve an amendment to the Company’s Certificate of Incorporation to reflect Delaware law provisions allowing officer exculpation. Approval requires the affirmative vote of a majority of the shares outstanding on the record date. Abstentions and broker non-votes have the same effect as votes against the proposal.

items.title: Election of six director nominees for one-year terms
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to elect Zachary K. Bradford, S. Matthew Schultz, Larry McNeill, Dr. Thomas Wood, Roger Beynon, and Amanda Cavaleri as directors to hold office until the next annual meeting or until their successors are elected and qualified. Directors are elected by a plurality of votes cast. Only votes FOR affect the outcome; withheld votes and broker non-votes have no effect.
items.approvalStandard: The plurality of the votes cast

items.title: Approval of certificate of amendment to increase authorized shares of Common Stock
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve an amendment to the Articles of Incorporation to increase the number of authorized shares of Common Stock from 100,000,000 to 300,000,000 shares. Approval requires the affirmative vote of a majority of the outstanding shares. Abstentions and broker non-votes have the same effect as votes against this proposal. Broker discretionary voting is allowed for this routine matter.
items.approvalStandard: The affirmative vote of the holders of a majority of the outstanding shares

items.title: Approval of amendment to 2017 Incentive Plan to increase shares and add evergreen provision
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve an amendment to the 2017 Incentive Plan to increase authorized shares from 3,500,000 to 11,512,000 and add an evergreen provision to automatically increase shares available to 15% of outstanding shares twice a year. Approval requires a majority of votes cast. Abstentions and broker non-votes do not affect the outcome.

items.title: Advisory vote to approve named executive officer compensation
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve, on a non-binding advisory basis, the compensation of named executive officers as disclosed in the proxy statement. Approval requires a majority of votes cast. Abstentions and broker non-votes do not affect the outcome. This vote is advisory and not binding.

items.title: Ratification of selection of MaloneBailey, LLP as independent registered public accounting firm
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to ratify the appointment of MaloneBailey, LLP as the independent registered public accounting firm for fiscal year ending September 30, 2023. Approval requires a majority of votes cast. Abstentions and broker non-votes do not affect the outcome. Broker discretionary voting is allowed for this routine matter.

items.title: Election of 12 directors to hold office until the next annual meeting of stockholders and until their respective successors have been elected and qualified
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to elect 12 directors to the Board to hold office until the next annual meeting and until their successors are elected and qualified. The Board recommends voting FOR each nominee.

items.title: Ratification of the selection of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent public accountants for fiscal year ending September 24, 2023
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to ratify the selection of PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as the Company's independent public accountants for the fiscal year ending September 24, 2023. The Board recommends voting FOR this proposal.

items.title: Approval of the QUALCOMM Incorporated 2023 Long-Term Incentive Plan
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve the QUALCOMM Incorporated 2023 Long-Term Incentive Plan, which will increase the number of shares available for equity awards by 82,000,000 shares and serve as a successor to the 2016 Long-Term Incentive Plan. The Board recommends voting FOR this proposal.

items.title: Approval, on an advisory basis, of the compensation of the named executive officers
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve, on an advisory basis, the compensation of the Company's named executive officers. The Board recommends voting FOR this proposal.

items.title: Approval of the sale of Rotor Riot, LLC and Fat Shark Holdings, Ltd. to Unusual Machines, Inc
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve the sale of Rotor Riot, LLC and Fat Shark Holdings, Ltd., each a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, to Unusual Machines, Inc. pursuant to a Share Purchase Agreement dated November 21, 2022. The total purchase price is $18 million in cash, notes, and stock. The Company's CEO, Jeffrey Thompson, who is also a significant stockholder of both companies, will abstain from voting on this proposal. The Board unanimously recommends a vote FOR this proposal. Approval requires a majority of votes cast by disinterested shares, excluding votes held by Jeffrey Thompson.
items.approvalStandard: Majority of votes cast by disinterested shares

items.title: Approval of adjournment of the Special Meeting, if necessary, to solicit additional proxies
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve an adjournment of the Special Meeting, if necessary, to solicit additional proxies if there are not sufficient votes in favor of the proposal to approve the sale of Rotor Riot and Fat Shark. The Board recommends a vote FOR this proposal. Approval requires the affirmative vote of a majority of the shares present in person or by proxy and entitled to vote on the matter. Abstentions count as votes against this proposal, and broker non-votes have no effect.
items.approvalStandard: Majority of shares present in person or by proxy and entitled to vote

items.title: Election of ten directors to serve for a one-year term
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to elect ten directors to serve for a one-year term and until their successors have been duly elected and qualified. The Board has nominated ten individuals currently serving as directors. Each director will serve until the 2024 Annual Meeting or until their successor is elected or earlier death, resignation, or removal.

items.summary: A shareholder proposal requesting that the Board take steps to give the owners of 10% of the outstanding common stock the power to call a special shareholder meeting.

items.summary: A shareholder proposal to improve the executive compensation program and policy to include the CEO pay ratio factor.

items.title: Election of Directors
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to elect nine directors: James Bell, Tim Cook, Al Gore, Alex Gorsky, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Monica Lozano, Ron Sugar, and Sue Wagner. All directors are elected annually for a one-year term under a majority voting standard in uncontested elections.

items.title: Ratification of Appointment of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to ratify the appointment of Ernst & Young LLP as Apple’s independent registered public accounting firm for 2023. The Audit Committee has re-appointed Ernst & Young LLP after considering their independence, performance, and communication quality.

items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve, on an advisory basis, the compensation paid to Apple’s named executive officers as disclosed in the proxy statement, including the Compensation Discussion and Analysis and executive compensation tables. The vote is advisory and not binding but will be considered by the Compensation Committee and Board in future decisions.

items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on how often advisory votes on executive compensation should be held: every one, two, or three years. The Board recommends holding the advisory vote every year to allow shareholders to express their views annually.

items.title: Civil Rights and Non-Discrimination Audit Proposal
items.summary: A shareholder proposal requesting a second civil rights audit, which the Board opposes as redundant and unnecessary given the ongoing Civil Rights Audit.

items.title: Communist China Audit
items.summary: A shareholder proposal requesting additional audits related to operations in China, which the Board opposes, citing existing extensive reporting and active Board oversight of risks related to China operations.

items.title: Board Policy
items.summary: A shareholder proposal to amend Board communication policy, which the Board opposes as overly prescriptive and potentially detrimental to effective shareholder engagement.

items.title: Racial and Gender Pay Gaps
items.summary: A shareholder proposal addressing pay equity, which the Board opposes, citing Apple’s comprehensive pay equity approach and transparency on representation and pay equity progress.

items.title: Shareholder Proxy Access Amendments
items.summary: A shareholder proposal to amend proxy access bylaws, which the Board opposes, noting existing robust proxy access provisions and lack of shareholder demand for changes.

items.title: Approval of amendment to increase the number of authorized shares of Common Stock
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve an amendment to the Certificate of Incorporation to increase the total number of authorized shares of Common Stock from 524,173,073 to 550,000,000 shares. This increase is necessary to enable the conversion of Series A Preferred Stock and AMC Preferred Equity Units (APEs) into Common Stock and to provide flexibility for future issuances.

items.title: Approval of amendment to effectuate a reverse stock split of Common Stock at a ratio of one-for-ten
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve an amendment to the Certificate of Incorporation to effectuate a reverse stock split of the Common Stock at a ratio of one share for every ten shares. This reverse split, together with the share increase, will enable the full conversion of Series A Preferred Stock and APEs into Common Stock and is intended to increase the stock price and attract institutional investors.

items.title: Approval of one or more adjournments of the Special Meeting if necessary
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve one or more adjournments of the Special Meeting, if necessary, to permit further solicitation of proxies if there are not sufficient votes at the time of the Special Meeting to approve and adopt the Charter Amendment Proposals (the share increase and reverse split proposals).

items.title: Stockholder Proposal Requesting a Report on Reducing Full Value Chain GHG Emissions
items.summary: A stockholder proposal requests a report on reducing greenhouse gas emissions across the Company's full value chain. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating that the proposal ignores the unique circumstances of the industry regarding Scope 3 emissions and that the Company's sustainability strategy continues to yield results and effectively mitigates risk.

The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating that stockholders already have a meaningful right to call special meetings and that the current ownership thresholds reflect strong corporate governance practices.

items.summary: A stockholder proposal requests that the Board amend its director election resignation bylaw to require directors who fail to receive majority vote support in uncontested elections to tender irrevocable resignations that the Board must accept absent compelling reasons. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating that current policies already provide significant accountability, the proposal is overly prescriptive, and the Board needs discretion to act in the best interests of the Company.

items.title: Stockholder Proposal: Board Corporate Financial Sustainability Committee
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve the creation of a Board Corporate Financial Sustainability Committee. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, believing there is already effective Board and committee oversight of social and political policy positions and their impact on financial sustainability, and that Intel provides extensive disclosure on the topic.

items.title: Stockholder Proposal: Risk Report of Opposing State Abortion Regulation
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve a report on risks related to opposing state abortion regulation. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, believing Intel offers competitive compensation, healthcare coverage, and benefits, and has robust governance processes to oversee risk and compliance, making the proposal unnecessary and not beneficial.

items.title: Stockholder Proposal: Policy for Excessive Golden Parachutes Approval
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to approve a policy requiring stockholder approval for excessive golden parachutes. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, citing that Intel already has a Cash Severance Policy addressing these concerns, that the proposal may restrict Compensation Committee flexibility, discourage long-term equity awards, and put Intel at a competitive disadvantage for recruiting and retaining executives.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding bylaw amendment: stockholder approval of director compensation
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal to amend the bylaws to require stockholder approval of director compensation. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating it is overly restrictive, not legally required, inconsistent with market practice, and would place the company at a competitive disadvantage.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding an EEO policy risk report
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a report on potential risks to the company of omitting “viewpoint” and “ideology” from the EEO Policy. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company’s commitment to a respectful, safe, inclusive workplace is already embedded across policies and trainings, and the report would not provide meaningful additional benefit.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a report on electromagnetic radiation and wireless technologies risks
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a report on risks related to electromagnetic radiation and wireless technologies. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company’s cellular devices meet all regulatory and safety requirements, and current regulatory limits are backed by scientific research showing no established adverse health effects below exposure limits.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a policy for director transparency on political and charitable giving
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a policy for director transparency on political and charitable giving. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company already has a robust governance framework and that mandating public disclosure may deter qualified individuals from serving on the Board.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a report on climate risks to retirement plan beneficiaries
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a report on climate risks to retirement plan beneficiaries. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the 401(k) Plan participants can invest in a wide range of investments and that federal law requires fiduciaries to make investment decisions based on relevant risk-return factors, cautioning against undue pressure focusing narrowly on climate risks.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a lobbying report
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a lobbying report. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company already publishes extensive lobbying disclosures and has robust oversight mechanisms in place.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding equal shareholder voting
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal regarding equal shareholder voting. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the current capital structure and governance practices have provided significant long-term stability and benefits to stockholders.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a report on reproductive healthcare misinformation risks
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a report on reproductive healthcare misinformation risks. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company has clear policies governing abortion-related advertising and strives to protect users from misleading content.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding AI principles and Board oversight
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal regarding AI principles and Board oversight. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating oversight of AI risks is already effectively carried out at the full Board and Audit and Compliance Committee levels, and explicitly calling out AI in the committee charter is unnecessary.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a report on generative AI misinformation and disinformation risks
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a report on generative AI misinformation and disinformation risks. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company has enterprise risk frameworks and policies to identify and mitigate AI-generated misinformation and is transparent about ongoing work.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a human rights assessment of AI-driven targeted ad policies
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a human rights assessment of AI-driven targeted ad policies. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company has effective human rights governance and has progressed privacy-enhancing solutions.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a report on online safety for children
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a report on online safety for children. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company builds child-appropriate features into products and provides extensive information and metrics on child safety.

items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal regarding support for shareholder right to act by written consent. items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding an enhanced disclosure on climate goals
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting enhanced disclosure on climate goals. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company has a long track record of transparency and already provides information about climate goals, progress, policies, and practices in existing environmental reporting.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding equal shareholder voting
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal regarding equal shareholder voting. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the current capital structure has provided significant long-term stability and growth, and that strong governance and independent board leadership hold management accountable.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a report on the due diligence process to assess human rights risks in CAHRA
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a report on the due diligence process to assess human rights risks in CAHRA. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company’s human rights governance and management structure provides effective oversight of key human rights risks and mitigation strategies, and policies are regularly reviewed.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a report on risks of discrimination in GenAI
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a report on risks of discrimination in GenAI. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company publishes AI Responsibility reports and technical reports addressing these concerns, emphasizing neutral and universal design principles.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a report on AI data usage oversight
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a report on AI data usage oversight. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company’s AI and data governance frameworks and privacy policies provide comprehensive oversight, and the company collaborates with the broader ecosystem to advance privacy standards and mitigate risks.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a human rights impact assessment of AI-driven targeted ad policies
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a human rights impact assessment of AI-driven targeted ad policies. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company’s human rights governance provides effective oversight and that privacy-enhancing technologies address similar concerns.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a report on alignment of lobbying activities with child safety policies
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a report on alignment of lobbying activities with child safety policies. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company has published a legislative framework to protect children and believes the requested report is unnecessary.

items.title: Stockholder proposal regarding a report on online safety for children
items.summary: Stockholders are asked to vote on a proposal requesting a report on online safety for children. The Board recommends voting against this proposal, stating the company has strong policies and extensive steps to protect children, provides other voluntary disclosures, and regulatory frameworks include robust reporting requirements.
